result.summary: The page is largely well-composed, but the promotional banner has a serious contrast problem: white headline and subtext on a pale green background are barely legible. Other elements (header, chips, carousels, bottom nav) appear intentional and functional; partial visibility of the last carousel card and the bottom card are expected scroll behaviors.

issues.description: In the '3 free deliveries for you' promo banner, the white heading and the 'Use code TALLINN3 at checkout · min. order €10' subtext sit on a very light mint-green background, resulting in extremely low contrast that makes the text hard to read.
issues.suggestion: Use a darker green background (or darker text color) so the banner text meets WCAG AA contrast ratios, e.g. deep green background with white text or light background with dark green text.

issues.description: The 'Order now' button inside the promo banner uses green text on a white pill, which is fine, but the banner's low-contrast text makes the call-to-code information (TALLINN3) easy to miss, reducing the promo's effectiveness.
issues.suggestion: Emphasize the promo code with a bold/monospace chip or higher-contrast styling so users can notice and copy the code.
